name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in CI with a dry-run mode for a week, then enforce rules. The trade-off is temporary noise in PRs while we validate the rules don’t block real work. This beats pre-commit because CI catches issues across all contributors, not just local commits.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent in CI with dry-run risks two failures: first, it normalizes noise in PRs as "temporary," but reviewers will still ignore or override it, making the dry-run meaningless; second, it assumes "safe" is objective, but rules that block real work reveal that "safe" is just what the enforcer allows. A better alternative is to run PR-Agent on a random 10% of PRs without any enforcement, measure the actual impact on review time and merge rates, then decide whether to scale. Settle the argument by running a controlled experiment for two weeks and comparing metrics before/after.
